thread:
Holly F: Heads-up  Neon Health reached out: they say their March invoice INV-2027-03-30-NH shows mix of legacy experimental pricing and new public pricing for the same SKU. They were part of a pricing experiment and expected a billing-aligned retro credit for the experiment period. Can finance ops look?

billing-bot: Invoice INV-2027-03-30-NH posted 2027-03-30 08:02Z. Total: $34,120.75. Status: paid. PDF: https://billing.redwood.internal/invoices/INV-2027-03-30-NH

Mark S (Sales): Customer was enrolled in "experiment-pricing-jan-mar" which gave $0.004/token on usage vs new standard $0.0035/token. The experiment was supposed to be billed at experiment rate for March usage with a retro adjustment applied after experiment end. Looks like system billed half the March usage at new public rate and half at legacy experiment rate.

Holly F: Pasted invoice lines export:
```
acct,desc,period,qty,unit_price,line_total
NH-501,Tokens - infer,2027-03,5,000,000,0.0035,17,500.00
NH-501,Tokens - infer (exp),2027-03,5,000,000,0.0040,20,000.00
NH-501,Support - premium,2027-03,1,500.00,1,500.00
```
Seems like duplicate partition: same usage split across two lines with different unit prices. The experiment owner expected all March usage to be billed at experiment price (0.0040) with a post-hoc credit if the final experience required an effective blended price. The customer is asking for a clear reconciled invoice.

Devon (Pricing): Looking at experiment logs: experiment flagging sent both to legacy-meter and new-pricing-service during a shard migration on 2027-03-15. That generated split reporting. Pricing policy for experiments says we should reconcile to the experiment intent: bill at experiment rate and, if necessary, apply a retro credit if finance policy dictates. Neon Health contract clause: "If experiment triggers different public price, customer receives invoice reconciliation with adjustment to match agreed experiment pricing for the period."

Holly F: Quick math: combined token qty = 10,000,000. If billed entirely at experiment rate 0.0040 -> 40,000.00. Current combined on invoice = 37,500.00 (17,500 + 20,000? wait that sum is 37,500). But invoice total before support shows 37,500. So customer was underbilled relative to experiment expectation by 2,500. But the customer claims they were promised a guarantee of experiment price which in this case was higher so they expected to be billed the higher amount? They actually are asking for reconciliation because their contract states the experiment pricing should be applied uniformly; they want corrected invoice (either credit or debit) and explanation for auditors.

Mark S (Sales): Contract note: experiment-pricing-jan-mar "customer will be billed at whichever price is more favorable to Redwood, with reconciliations to align to announced experiment outcome." Oops, that language favors Redwood. But sales escalated asking we follow the agreed internal experiment settlement (we agreed to bill at the higher of the two and then automatically credit if experiment failed to meet metrics). However the customer signed a separate addendum that expects consolidated billing. We need legal and finance review.

Priya (Dir Finance): Thanks for context. Two items: 1) operational fix to prevent split lines (eng-billing); 2) accounting treatment for the reconciliation. If the experiment intent was to bill at experiment rate and the invoice is inconsistent, we should reissue a reconciled invoice. If the reconciled amount is more than paid, we need direction on collecting incremental amount; if less, we issue credit. But policy is to avoid surprise debits to customers after invoice without clear consent. We should contact customer ASAP to confirm they accept reconciled invoice if it increases charge. For Neon, I recommend we honor the lower billed amount (don't ask for additional payment) and instead log an internal adjustment to reflect experiment accounting. But check contract/legal.

Devon (Pricing): From experiment admin: the intended behavior was to apply the experiment price to all March usage and then run a settlement step. Due to the shard migration we have a partial double-write; we should stop collecting partials and ensure future billing uses single source of truth. Will open bug.

Holly F: Customer reached out saying they'd prefer clarity and asked for a single reconciled invoice. They do NOT want an unexpected additional charge; they'd rather see a credit or an invoice note.

Priya (Dir Finance): Given customer preference and to avoid disputes, we will not invoice additional amount. We will issue an internal revenue true-up so net customer-facing impact is zero increase. Action: 1) create reconciliation memo that reclassifies the two price lines into a single line at the lower of the two prices for customer billing (i.e., keep posted invoice as-is to respect payment), 2) create internal journal entry to reflect the experiment variance between billed amount and experiment accounting; 3) produce customer-facing corrected invoice that aggregates lines but keeps net amount at $37,500 and includes explanatory note: "Billing reconciliation due to pricing experiment migration; no additional charge." Approve manual credit memo if needed to remove one of the duplicate lines for clarity.

Holly F: Proposed action: create CM-2027-2705 for -20,000.00 to remove the experiment-priced line and then create a reissued invoice INV-2027-03-30-NH-R1 showing a single line Tokens - infer 10,000,000 @ 0.00375 = 37,500.00 (blended for clarity) and support 1,500.00. That leaves posted customer amount unchanged. Internal accounting will book the experiment delta (40,000 expected vs 37,500 billed) as an internal adjustment FIN-EXP-2027-11. Need Dir Finance sign-off for CM on a paid invoice and the internal true-up.

Priya (Dir Finance): I approve the approach. Use adj code FIN-EXP-2027-11 for internal experiment settlement and create credit memo to tidy the external invoice. Ensure GL entries: Revenue Contra 4010 for -20,000 on the CM, then reissue invoice metadata linking to original payment. Book experiment variance to Other R&D expense 8340 or to a designated experiment clearing GL per policy; Devon please confirm GL.

Devon (Pricing): Confirming GL for experiment settlement: use Experiment Clearing 4999 for the variance, then periodic close will move to R&D if appropriate. I'll add note to BI-2027-88 (billing migration bug) and include sample event ids.

billing-bot: Created credit memo CM-2027-2705 amount -20000.00 and applied to INV-2027-03-30-NH. Status: applied. Reference FIN-EXP-2027-11.

eng-billing-bot: Created BI-2027-88 with title "pricing-service/legacy-meter double-write on shard migration" and assigned to eng-billing. Added unit test 'experiment_single_source' to prevent split billing.

Holly F: Reissued invoice INV-2027-03-30-NH-R1 showing blended token line 10,000,000 @ 0.00375 = 37,500.00 and Support 1,500.00. Total unchanged 39,000.00 (including support). Sent to customer with note: "No additional charge; reconciled for clarity due to internal migration. Contact for any questions."

Lena (Payments): No refund or charge needed; customer payment applied to original invoice remains valid. Mark CM as customer-visible clarifying credit only.

Mark S (Sales): Customer replied: thanks for clarity, appreciate proactive handling. They requested an internal write-up for auditors; attaching the reissued invoice will suffice.

Holly F: Closing after eng-billing confirms bug assignment and finance posts internal experiment clearing entries.

Devon (Pricing): I'll coordinate with accounting on FIN-EXP-2027-11 and close BI-2027-88 once tests pass.

Priya (Dir Finance): Thanks team. Please add FIN-EXP-2027-11 to monthly manual adjustments report and tag as non-cash experiment settlement.

Holly F: Closing thread.
